Cybersecurity Incident Forces Turning Stone's New York Casinos to Go Cash-Only

Published November 3, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Turning Stone Enterprises, the commercial arm of the Oneida Nation, is investigating a cybersecurity incident that has disrupted systems across its properties in central New York, forcing Turning Stone Resort Casino in Verona, Point Place Casino in Bridgeport, and YBR Casino & Sports Book in Chittenango to go cash-only. The company reported the incident on Monday and shut down selected internal systems as a precaution while it investigates.

What's offline

Credit cards are not being accepted at the affected properties, and ATMs remain offline. TS Sports, the company's sports betting operation, did not open Tuesday, and bingo operations are also unavailable. The incident knocked out TS Rewards, the loyalty program patrons use to earn and redeem points on gambling, hotel stays, and dining. Cash-only restrictions also extend to The Lake House at Sylvan Beach and the company's Maple Leaf Markets and SavOn convenience stores. The casinos themselves, along with those other businesses, remained open on cash-only terms rather than closing outright.

What the company has said

Joel Barkin, Turning Stone Enterprises' vice president for strategic communications and community engagement, said: "We are working rapidly with top cybersecurity experts to assess the nature and scope of the incident and assist with our response." He added, "Protecting confidential information is our highest priority. We will provide additional information as we have it." The company said it has found no evidence that any confidential information was accessed, though its investigation is ongoing, and it has not identified a cause or said whether a third party was responsible. Turning Stone has committed to sending daily email updates and posting a nightly update until the issue is resolved, directing guests to check its website and Facebook page; no restoration timeline has been given.

Why it matters

Tribal gaming operations have increasingly been targeted by cybersecurity incidents in recent years, and a multi-day disruption to payment systems, a sportsbook, and a loyalty program at a casino of Turning Stone's size is a reminder of how much of a modern casino's day-to-day operation — not just online betting, but on-property cash handling and rewards tracking — now runs through connected systems that can fail all at once. For players with visits planned at any of the affected properties, the practical takeaway for now is simple: bring cash, don't expect to earn or redeem TS Rewards points, and don't expect to bet with TS Sports until the company confirms systems are back online.
